result.result:
The app is built and every flow works in a real browser, but I couldn't compare it against Figma: the Figma token is expired. Both the MCP server and a direct API call returned `403 Token expired`, so I never saw the frames. The layout and badge colours are my guesses from the spec and the design system's own styling, not matched to Figma.

**What I checked:** I ran the whole flow in headless Chromium at 1440px and 390px wide, and the console stayed clean throughout.
- Login shows required-field errors on an empty submit, `admin`/`admin` reaches `/dashboard`, and the guards redirect both ways.
- The dashboard has all 8 tiles, and the log panel adds a line every 3 seconds.
- The profile menu opens leftward and stays fully on screen at both widths. It closes on an outside click, and Sign Out returns to `/login`.
- Create, edit and delete all go through the in-memory API, and the table updates each time.
- All four dialogs open and close, and the delete confirmation also closes on a backdrop click. Edit's "Delete user" opens the confirmation with the same member still selected.
- `ng build` passes with no errors or warnings. `npx @angular/cli@19 serve` starts it.

**Guesses that need a Figma check:**
- **Dashboard layout:** four metric tiles on the first row, then the other four tiles two per row.
- **Badge colours:** Admin dark, Editor blue, Viewer grey; Active green, Inactive grey.
- **Brand and footer:** the brand name "Blueprint", the header's built-in default logo, and the footer link columns are placeholders.
- **Joined column:** shows the raw date, e.g. `2024-01-15`.

**Gaps in the component library:**
- **No place for the profile control in the header.** The library header can't hold extra content, so I built the profile control myself and placed it over the header's right edge. Below about 450px wide it overlaps the nav links. I left the name visible because the spec says it must always show.
- **Dropdown cut off inside dialogs.** The dialog body scrolls, which clipped the Role dropdown's options. My fix, in `src/styles.css`, turns off body scrolling for the edit and invite dialogs only. It targets one of the library's internal class names, so a library update could break it. The catch: on a very short screen those two dialogs can't scroll.
- **Header links reload the page.** They're plain links, so the layout routes them through the Angular router. Otherwise every nav click would reload the app and reset the in-memory data.
- **No image fallback.** The avatar shows initials only when there is no image URL, not when the image fails to load.

**Arm B protocol issue:** the installed `@jablonowski/dsb-components` package includes `llms.client.txt`, and its README points to it. The protocol says arm B shouldn't have that file, so I didn't read it. I worked only from the READMEs, the type definitions and the compiled source. Other arm-B runs may have read it, so the B vs C comparison may not be clean.

To finish the visual pass, refresh `FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN` and I can compare against frames `22-11104`, `22:11448` and `22:11492` and adjust spacing and layout.
